tagline: Home of the Bang Rachan heroes, Mae La snakehead fish, and old temples along the Chao Phraya River
introHtml:
Sing Buri is a small central-plains province on the Chao Phraya River, and most people picture two things first: the Bang Rachan heroes who stood and fought until the story became part of the town's identity, and Mae La snakehead fish, famous for firm, sweet flesh and now the local dish people come for. The town isn't far from Ang Thong and Lopburi, so you can drive in for a day trip and head home by evening, or string it together with the nearby provinces for an easy two-day temple run.

Beyond the history, Sing Buri has plenty of old temples scattered along the river, including Wat Phra Non Chakkrasi with its long reclining Buddha and Wat Phikun Thong with its huge Buddha image. In between it's rice fields and orchards, one after another. It's an unhurried province: see the temples, hear the Bang Rachan story, then track down Mae La snakehead fish and roadside local food without rushing.
bestTime: November–February, cool and comfortable, when you can visit temples and drive along the Chao Phraya River all day without the heat

highlights.name: Bang Rachan Heroes Memorial Park
highlights.blurb: A monument and memorial ground for the Bang Rachan villagers who rose up to fight. It's the town's defining story, and people come to Sing Buri specifically to see it and hear the history.

highlights.name: Wat Phra Non Chakkrasi Worawihan
highlights.blurb: An old temple with a long reclining Buddha enshrined in the hall. It's the town's important reclining Buddha, and people come to pay respects and make a wish.

highlights.name: Mae La snakehead fish
highlights.blurb: Snakehead fish from the Mae La River, famous for firm, sweet flesh. It's the local dish that many people come all the way here to eat.

highlights.name: Wat Phikun Thong (Luang Pho Phae)
highlights.blurb: A temple with a large Buddha image, home of Luang Pho Phae, a revered monk. It's one of the town's main places to pay respects.

highlights.name: Ban Khu Mueang Ancient Town
highlights.blurb: Traces of a Dvaravati-era town where artifacts have been unearthed, showing that people settled this area a very long time ago.

highlights.name: Life along the Chao Phraya River
highlights.blurb: Sing Buri is low-lying floodplain by the Chao Phraya. Drive along the river past temples, rice fields, and orchards, and you'll see everyday local life at an easy pace.

foodScene.name: Mae La snakehead fish
foodScene.note: Sing Buri's most famous dish: firm-fleshed snakehead from the Mae La River, grilled, in tom yum, or fried with fish sauce at roadside spots.

foodScene.name: River fish and river prawns
foodScene.note: A town on the Chao Phraya means fresh freshwater fish and river prawns, grilled or in tom yum, plus grilled prawns at the riverside spots.

foodScene.name: Boat noodles (kuay teow reua)
foodScene.note: Sing Buri sits in the central region's boat-noodle belt, with small bowls of strong, rich broth that you order a few at a time along the road.

foodScene.name: Thai sweets and local souvenirs
foodScene.note: Markets and shops around town carry traditional Thai sweets and local products to take home.

foodScene.name: Isan food
foodScene.note: Som tam, grilled chicken, and laap are easy to find all over town and along the road, with bold flavors that travelers like.

foodScene.name: Mu krata (DIY grilled pork)
foodScene.note: A popular dinner for locals, with several places to choose from, a relaxed feel, and friendly prices.

foodScene.name: Beef noodles and made-to-order dishes
foodScene.note: In town you'll find long-running beef-noodle shops and made-to-order spots for an easy meal at local prices.

foodScene.name: Cafes in town and by the river
foodScene.note: There are small cafes in the town center and along the river to sit and sip coffee after temple visits.

attractions.name: Bang Rachan Heroes Memorial Park
attractions.blurb: A memorial ground for the Bang Rachan villagers who rose up to fight, with a monument and buildings that tell the history. It's the main draw for people coming to Sing Buri.

attractions.name: Wat Phra Non Chakkrasi Worawihan
attractions.blurb: An old temple with a long reclining Buddha in the hall, the town's important reclining Buddha, where people regularly stop to pay respects and make a wish.

attractions.name: Wat Phikun Thong
attractions.blurb: A temple with a large Buddha image, home of Luang Pho Phae, a revered monk, with a wide, shady, peaceful setting.

attractions.name: Wat Sawang Arom
attractions.blurb: A temple known for Buddha-image sculpting and casting; you can watch the craftsmen at work and pay respects to the main Buddha image.

attractions.name: Ban Khu Mueang Ancient Town
attractions.blurb: A Dvaravati-era archaeological site where artifacts have been unearthed, with a small museum that tells the story of the area's earliest people.

attractions.name: Wat Pho Kao Ton
attractions.blurb: An old temple near the Bang Rachan camp tied to the heroes' story, with old bodhi trees and a quiet feel for a stop to pay respects.

attractions.name: Ban Rachan Retro Thai Market
attractions.blurb: A community market with a retro feel, with local food and souvenirs. It's a pleasant place to graze and watch everyday local life.

attractions.name: Chao Phraya riverside and rice fields
attractions.blurb: The Chao Phraya floodplain is full of rice fields and orchards. Drive or cycle along the river to take in everyday local life at an easy pace.
